quirks.condition: Any revaluation reply line for a book.
quirks.effect: The revaluation path computes each pair's value as floored integer tenths of a cent, sums the tenths across the whole book, and rounds the total once half-up to cents; the trade path rounds each pair separately half-even to cents and sums, so the same state can print one cent apart between the two paths. The spec applies the trade path's per-pair half-even rounding to both.

quirks.condition: A trade that carries a pair's signed position from strictly positive to strictly negative or the reverse.
quirks.effect: The stored last rate for that pair becomes the trade's rate minus 5 tenths of a pip, and every later net value uses the reduced rate until the pair is retraded or refixed. The spec stores the trade's rate unchanged.

quirks.condition: A pair whose last three letters are JPY, valued on the trade path or on a revaluation whose fixing list names the pair.
quirks.effect: The pair's value is position times rate divided by 100 instead of 10000, so the printed cents are 100 times the spec formula's result.

quirks.condition: A revaluation whose fixing list does not name a held JPY-quoted pair.
quirks.effect: That pair is revalued with the 10000 divisor on its stale rate rather than the 100 divisor used for it everywhere else, so the book's revaluation net value drops by a factor of 100 on that pair's contribution relative to the preceding trade reply.

quirks.condition: A trade that brings a pair's position to exactly zero.
quirks.effect: The pair is removed from the book and its last rate is forgotten; no rate adjustment is applied, and a later trade on that pair starts from a fresh position. The spec keeps the flat pair on the book with its last rate.

quirks.condition: A T command whose amount token is all zeros (such as 0 or 00) and whose other fields pass validation, including a nonzero rate.
quirks.effect: The command is dropped silently: no reply line, no book or rate change, and no increment to the trade or reject counters in the trailer. A zero amount with a zero rate still rejects RATE. The spec rejects a zero amount with AMT.

quirks.condition: A book id that differs only in letter case from a book already seen in the session.
quirks.effect: It is treated as the same book: positions merge, the first-seen spelling is echoed on every reply, and revaluations print one line for the merged book. The spec treats book ids as case-sensitive and distinct.

quirks.condition: A T command with more than six whitespace-separated tokens.
quirks.effect: The extra trailing tokens are ignored and the trade is applied from the first six tokens; the spec rejects the line with FMT. The V fixing list is unaffected and is still taken verbatim, so trailing junk there rejects FMT.

unmapped_families.reason: Two held-out mixed corpora of 155 or more commands with interleaved V lines that exercise every rule above together; no single quirk maps.

reader_questions.question: A fresh session receives exactly two commands: first "T bk1 EURUSD B 15 15000", then "V EURUSD=15000". What net value, in cents, does the engine print on the reply line for the V command?
reader_questions.verification: printf 'T bk1 EURUSD B 15 15000\nV EURUSD=15000\n' | .venv/bin/python builder/gold_hedgecore.py -> 'P bk1 22', 'P bk1 23', 'X 1 1 0'; repo/legacy/run gives the same three lines. The V reply 'P bk1 23' confirms the answer (the spec-faithful reading gives 22).

reader_questions.question: A fresh session receives the single command "T bk1 EURJPY B 50 1610". What net value, in cents, does the engine print on the reply line?
reader_questions.verification: printf 'T bk1 EURJPY B 50 1610\n' | .venv/bin/python builder/gold_hedgecore.py -> 'P bk1 805', 'X 1 0 0'; repo/legacy/run gives the same two lines. The reply 'P bk1 805' confirms the answer (the spec-faithful reading gives 8).
